text:
sam: Heads up — after the mkdocs->docusaurus migration I hit a broken anchor on /guides/auth. The link from /integrations/okta -> #session-persistence 404s in prod. Anyone seen this?

yasmine: yeah, saw that in the nightly run. linkcheck flagged it last night. Do we have a PR yet? @sam

sam: opened a tiny PR to add an explicit id to the heading and a redirect shim: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4512

claire: quick note — emoji in headings (e.g. '🔒 Session') are slugified differently between mkdocs and docusaurus which will break fragment links. Prefer adding an explicit id like `## Session {#session-persistence}` when the heading contains emoji or special chars.

mike: I can take the mkdocs.yml redirect change + add a test in the linkcheck harness. Will branch as `fix/auth-anchor`.

docs-bot: buildkite/docs-validate #987 failed: linkcheck found missing fragment `/integrations/okta#session-persistence`

mike: pushed WIP — added a redirect map and fixed the heading id. snippet I added to the PR: 
```yaml
plugins:
  - redirects:
      redirect_maps:
        'integrations/okta/index.md':
          - from: 'integrations/okta#session-persistence'
            to: 'integrations/okta#session-management'
```

sam: small nit — mapping to a different anchor name can hide the underlying slug inconsistency and leave other inbound links broken. Better: add a canonical explicit id in the target doc and update inbound links to use that id. I can sweep the handful of pages that point to the old slug in one commit.

yasmine: ran a local docusaurus build (`npm run build && npm run serve`) and verified the anchor jump works after the explicit id. Marking PR ready for review.

claire: :thumbsup: happy to review. I'll also watch the CI linkcheck run once merged.

mike: merged the branch, CI linkcheck passed on 1768802520 — no more missing fragments reported. cc @sam @yasmine

sam: thanks! Leaving a note for the release notes: "Fix: normalize session heading anchors (avoid emoji-only slugs); add redirects for legacy links."

claire: tiny follow-up: let's add a short docs styleguide blurb under "Writing docs" that recommends explicit header ids for any heading containing emoji, inline code or non-ascii punctuation. Saves future surprises.

yasmine: agreed. I'll open a follow-up PR with the styleguide tweak and a small linkcheck test to catch emoji-slug regressions.

sam: perfect — thanks everyone.
